newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Banking sector pulls Moroccan bourse down.
newsitem.headline: Banking sector pulls Moroccan bourse down.

text.p: Banking and financial stocks pulled down the Casablanca stock market on Tuesday, the second consecutive fall after a week of gains, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed down at 427.17 points, down 0.45 percent on Monday's session.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc fell 20 dirhams to close at 720, with Credit Eqdom shares also falling 20 dirhams to 960.
Wafabank, one of the market's most liquid stocks, lost three dirhams to close at 500 dirhams.
A rise by Morocco's main brewery firm, Brasseries, of 41 dirhams to 1,380 was insufficient to counter the overall fall.

"The market index fall was expected as the market became more liquid...Investors are selling blocks shares to make profits mainly in blue chips shares including Banque Commerciale du Maroc which lost 20 dirhams in one session," Sanae Bennouna, an analyst at Upline Securities said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the largest market capitalisations, dropped 13 dirhams to close at 407 dirhams.
Upline Securities USI.CS index, which tracks the 10 most liquid stocks, closed at 55,488 points, down 0.16 percent on the previous session.

Societe Nationale d'Investissment, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies, was the only blue chip whose price remained stable at 600 dirhams, Bennouna added. The total bourse traded volume was 27 million dirhams, compared with 32 million dirhams on Monday.
